I am an old man with no schooling, but I have farmed these lands all my life. This quarter-hectare of rice is near the wetland edge, so the soil stays moist enough without me needing to irrigate. I have a few oxen and some manure, which I will spread on the plot before ploughing, and I will buy what urea and DAP I can afford from the cooperative — though they never give us enough. I will plant the seed I saved from last year, and my family will do most of the transplanting and weeding, but I will hire a few day-laborers when the harvest comes because my back is not what it used to be.
